NAME: Water
Description: A colorless liquid formed by two hydrogen atoms sharing electrons with one oxygen atom.
RealWorldApplication: Essential for all known forms of life; covers about 71% of Earth's surface and makes up roughly 60% of the human body.

NAME: Hydrogen Gas
Description: The simplest and lightest molecular gas, composed of two hydrogen atoms sharing a single covalent bond.
RealWorldApplication: Fuels the nuclear fusion in our Sun and is being developed as zero-emission green vehicle fuel.

NAME: Oxygen Gas
Description: A colorless, odorless diatomic gas that sustains aerobic cellular respiration and combustion.
RealWorldApplication: Makes up 21% of Earth's atmosphere and is breathed into human lungs to generate energy in cells.

NAME: Nitrogen Gas
Description: A super-stable diatomic molecule held together by a strong triple covalent bond.
RealWorldApplication: Comprises 78% of Earth's air and protects snack chips from going stale inside bags.

NAME: Chlorine Gas
Description: A greenish-yellow gas with a pungent odor, composed of two covalently bonded chlorine atoms.
RealWorldApplication: Used in municipal water treatment plants worldwide to kill harmful bacteria in drinking water.

NAME: Fluorine Gas
Description: An extremely reactive, pale yellow diatomic halogen gas.
RealWorldApplication: Its compounds prevent tooth decay and create super-slippery non-stick cookware coatings.

NAME: Ozone
Description: A triatomic molecule with a pungent smell that forms a protective layer in Earth's stratosphere.
RealWorldApplication: The stratospheric ozone layer absorbs 97-99% of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet rays.

NAME: Sodium Chloride
Description: An ionic crystal lattice where sodium transfers 1 electron to chlorine to achieve stable octets.
RealWorldApplication: Critical electrolyte in the human bloodstream and nervous system for nerve signal transmission.

NAME: Potassium Chloride
Description: An ionic salt composed of potassium cations and chloride anions.
RealWorldApplication: Supplies potassium necessary for healthy plant root growth and prevents muscle cramps in humans.

NAME: Magnesium Oxide
Description: A white ionic solid formed by electron transfer from magnesium to oxygen.
RealWorldApplication: Withstands temperatures up to 2,800°C, making it essential for lining steel-melting blast furnaces.

NAME: Calcium Oxide
Description: Also called quicklime, an alkaline ionic compound formed from calcium and oxygen.
RealWorldApplication: Core ingredient in manufacturing Portland cement that builds concrete bridges and buildings.

NAME: Calcium Chloride
Description: A hygroscopic ionic salt formed by one calcium atom and two chlorine atoms.
RealWorldApplication: Melts highway ice at lower temperatures than table salt by releasing heat when dissolving.

NAME: Magnesium Chloride
Description: An ionic halide salt highly soluble in water.
RealWorldApplication: The primary ingredient in traditional Japanese nigari used to solidify soy milk into tofu.

NAME: Carbon Dioxide
Description: A linear covalent molecule where carbon forms double bonds with two oxygen atoms.
RealWorldApplication: Green plants absorb CO₂ and water during photosynthesis to generate glucose and oxygen.

NAME: Carbon Monoxide
Description: A toxic, odorless, colorless gas formed during incomplete combustion of carbon fuels.
RealWorldApplication: Emitted by car exhausts and faulty heaters; home CO detectors warn against its toxic buildup.

NAME: Sulfur Dioxide
Description: A pungent, suffocating toxic gas released by volcanoes and burning fossil fuels.
RealWorldApplication: Primary cause of acid rain when it reacts with atmospheric moisture to form sulfurous acid.

NAME: Sulfur Trioxide
Description: A key chemical intermediate that vigorously reacts with water to form sulfuric acid.
RealWorldApplication: Central intermediate in the industrial Contact Process for producing high-grade sulfuric acid.

NAME: Nitric Oxide
Description: A free radical gas molecule that plays critical signaling roles in animal cardiovascular systems.
RealWorldApplication: Acts as a biological neurotransmitter causing blood vessels to dilate and lower blood pressure.

NAME: Nitrogen Dioxide
Description: A reddish-brown toxic gas with a biting odor, prominent in smog pollution.
RealWorldApplication: Key air pollutant produced by internal combustion engines that creates urban photochemical smog.

NAME: Nitrous Oxide
Description: Commonly known as laughing gas, a sweet-smelling covalent gas.
RealWorldApplication: Used safely by dentists as a mild pain reliever and sedative during dental procedures.

NAME: Methane
Description: A tetrahedral covalent molecule; the simplest hydrocarbon and main constituent of natural gas.
RealWorldApplication: Piped into kitchen stoves and water heaters as clean-burning natural gas.

NAME: Ethane
Description: The second-simplest alkane hydrocarbon gas.
RealWorldApplication: Cracked at high temperatures into ethylene to produce polyethylene plastic bottles and bags.

NAME: Ethylene
Description: An unsaturated hydrocarbon containing a carbon-carbon double bond; also a natural plant ripening hormone.
RealWorldApplication: Naturally released by bananas and apples that triggers nearby fruit to ripen faster.

NAME: Propane
Description: A three-carbon alkane gas easily compressed into a portable liquid.
RealWorldApplication: Stored in metal cylinders for outdoor barbecue grilling and mobile camping stoves.

NAME: Ammonia
Description: A trigonal pyramidal covalent gas with a pungent, recognizable odor.
RealWorldApplication: Provides the essential nitrogen fertilizer that sustains nearly half of global food production.

NAME: Hydrochloric Acid
Description: A binary polar covalent compound that ionizes completely in water to form gastric acid.
RealWorldApplication: Produced naturally in human stomachs to break down food proteins and kill ingested bacteria.

NAME: Hydrofluoric Acid
Description: A highly reactive acid capable of dissolving glass and silicate minerals.
RealWorldApplication: Used in high-tech cleanrooms to etch microscopic circuits onto computer microprocessor chips.

NAME: Sulfuric Acid
Description: A dense, oily mineral acid and the world's most widely produced industrial chemical.
RealWorldApplication: Serves as the liquid electrolyte inside 12V lead-acid car batteries that starts vehicle engines.

NAME: Nitric Acid
Description: A strong, oxidizing corrosive acid with a choking scent.
RealWorldApplication: Reacted with ammonia to create ammonium nitrate, feeding crops in modern agriculture.

NAME: Phosphoric Acid
Description: A triprotic acid commonly added to dark sodas for a tangy tart flavor.
RealWorldApplication: Gives cola soft drinks their crisp tangy kick and chemically converts orange rust into iron phosphate.

NAME: Carbonic Acid
Description: A weak acid formed when carbon dioxide gas dissolves into water.
RealWorldApplication: Maintains human blood pH precisely between 7.35 and 7.45 so enzymes continue functioning.

NAME: Hydrogen Peroxide
Description: A pale blue liquid containing an unstable oxygen-oxygen single peroxide bond.
RealWorldApplication: Bubbles and fizzes on cuts as enzymes break it down into harmless water and oxygen gas.

NAME: Sodium Hydroxide
Description: A caustic strong base known as lye, composed of sodium cations and hydroxide anions.
RealWorldApplication: Reacts with oils and fats in traditional soapmaking to create cleansing body and dish soaps.

NAME: Potassium Hydroxide
Description: Known as caustic potash, a powerful base used in liquid soaps and alkaline batteries.
RealWorldApplication: The conductive electrolyte solution inside everyday alkaline AA and AAA batteries.

NAME: Calcium Hydroxide
Description: Also called slaked lime, a basic powder made by adding water to quicklime.
RealWorldApplication: Spread across farm fields to neutralize soil acidity so crops can absorb nutrients effectively.

NAME: Magnesium Hydroxide
Description: A mild basic suspension famously known as Milk of Magnesia.
RealWorldApplication: Neutralizes excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach to quickly soothe heartburn and indigestion.

NAME: Calcium Carbonate
Description: A widespread mineral found in chalk, limestone, marble, and sea snail shells.
RealWorldApplication: Forms ocean coral reefs and sea snail shells, and is carved into magnificent marble statues.

NAME: Sodium Bicarbonate
Description: Everyday baking soda, an amphoteric salt that releases CO₂ gas when heated or mixed with acids.
RealWorldApplication: Releases carbon dioxide gas bubbles in cake and cookie batter, making baked goods light and fluffy.

NAME: Sodium Carbonate
Description: Commonly called washing soda, a water-soluble alkaline sodium salt.
RealWorldApplication: Acts as a flux in glass furnaces to lower silica melting temperature, saving tremendous energy.

NAME: Potassium Nitrate
Description: Also called saltpeter, a strong oxidizer used in pyrotechnics and plant nutrients.
RealWorldApplication: Calms nerve sensitivity in specialized toothpaste for sensitive teeth and enriches plant foliage.

NAME: Silicon Dioxide
Description: Also known as silica or quartz; the principal component of beach sand and window glass.
RealWorldApplication: Vibrates at an exact frequency (32,768 Hz) in quartz watches to keep precise time.

NAME: Aluminum Oxide
Description: An ultra-hard ceramic mineral occurring naturally as corundum, rubies, and sapphires.
RealWorldApplication: Forms the mineral base of red rubies (with trace chromium) and blue sapphires.

NAME: Iron(III) Oxide
Description: Common red rust formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water vapor.
RealWorldApplication: Gives the surface of the planet Mars and Australian outback sands their iconic red coloration.

NAME: Iron(II) Oxide
Description: A black-colored iron oxide powder used as a pigment and in chemical manufacturing.
RealWorldApplication: Used to produce heat-absorbing tinted green glass for automotive and architectural windows.

NAME: Zinc Oxide
Description: An insoluble white powder that reflects broad-spectrum UVA and UVB ultraviolet radiation.
RealWorldApplication: The safe, white physical UV blocker in mineral sunscreens that protects skin from sunburn.

NAME: Ethanol
Description: A volatile, flammable clear alcohol produced by yeast fermentation of sugars.
RealWorldApplication: The active antimicrobial agent in hospital hand sanitizers that instantly destroys viral membranes.

NAME: Acetic Acid
Description: A pungent organic carboxylic acid that gives household vinegar its sharp sour taste.
RealWorldApplication: Household white vinegar dissolves white hard-water mineral stains and limescale on faucets.

NAME: Glucose
Description: The primary simple monosaccharide sugar that fuels cellular metabolism in animals and plants.
RealWorldApplication: Circulates as blood sugar in the human body, supplying the primary energy fuel needed by brain neurons.
